newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade $64, moderate -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade $64, moderate -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle traded in moderate volume Friday at $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from fairly active sales this week, feedlot sources said.

Sales were estimated at 20,300 head in the Panhandle and 700 head in Kansas. Most showlists were sold this week, which kept feedlots current and spurred outlooks for steady-firm prices again next week, several cattle feeders said.
Weekly volume in the Panhandle was at 94,100 head and Kansas weekly movement was 93,600, USDA statistics showed.
Fed cattle prices were not expected to be impacted by Friday's USDA monthly cattle on feed report, they said.

The report was seen weighing slightly on CME August and October cattle futures because of larger than expected on-feed supplies as of July 1 and lower than expected marketings during June, industry analysts said.

USDA pegged on-feed supplies at 117 percent of a year ago, which was above analysts' pre-report average of 115.6 percent and marketings were at 102 percent, compared to the average estimate of 104 percent. June placements at 115 percent nearly matched the pre-report average of 115.5 percent.
